title: Cause of Recent LRT Train Breakdown, Progress of Upgrading Works and Expected Timeline for Resumption of Double Loop Service
what_it_is: Cause of Recent LRT Train Breakdown, Progress of Upgrading Works and Expected Timeline for Resumption of Double Loop Service

sections.label: Bukit Panjang LRT questions
sections.summary: Questions ask for updates on Bukit Panjang LRT upgrading, dual-loop resumption, train cabin replacement, a breakdown cause and mandated train checks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether he can provide an update on the progress of the upgrading works of the Bukit Panjang Light Rail Transit (LRT); and (b) when can the dual-loop service be fully resumed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) what is the current progress of the Bukit Panjang LRT upgrade project, particularly with regard to the resumption of the daily double loop service; and (b) what is the status of the replacement of the first-generation train cabins on the Bukit Panjang LRT line.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether an update can be provided on the cause of the recent LRT train breakdown between Bukit Panjang and Choa Chu Kang LRT stations; and (b) what regular checks are train operators mandated to conduct on LRT trains including on its tyres to prevent breakdowns.

sections.label: Gear failure cause
sections.summary: LTA's initial findings state the incident was caused by a gear failure in one wheel assembly of the incident train.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Based on the Land Transport Authority's (LTA's) initial findings, the incident was caused by a gear failure in one of the wheel assemblies of the incident train.

sections.label: Earlier shuttle service end
sections.summary: SMRT ended the shuttle train service along the affected stretch at about 10.00 pm to complete recovery works before next day's service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: To complete recovery works before service commencement the following day, SMRT decided to end the shuttle train service along the affected stretch earlier at around 10.00 pm, compared to the usual closing time of 11.30 pm.

sections.label: BPLRT early closure announcement
sections.summary: LTA announced early closure of the BPLRT from 14 November 2024 to 31 October 2025, with services ending an hour earlier Thursday to Sunday.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: To support these upgrading works, LTA recently announced the need for early closure of the BPLRT from 14 November 2024 to 31 October 2025, where train services would end one hour earlier every Thursday to Sunday, excluding public holidays.

sections.label: Commitment to expedite upgrading
sections.summary: The Minister commits to doing their best to expedite the upgrading works.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The commitment I want to give to Mr Liang and to the House is that we will do our best to expedite the upgrading works.

sections.label: Sengkang-Punggol LRT new trains
sections.summary: LTA procured 25 new two-car trains for Sengkang-Punggol LRT, with the first arriving in December and full two-car operation by mid-2028.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: To Ms Yeo's second question regarding the two-car trains to be added to the Sengkang-Punggol LRT, LTA has procured 25 new two-car trains for the Sengkang-Punggol LRT, with the first new two-car trains arriving in December this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: When all the new trains are delivered, it will double the number of two-car trains in the Sengkang-Punggol LRT fleet, which will allow the Sengkang-Punggol LRT to be operated entirely with two-car trains by mid-2028, increasing passenger capacity to better serve our residents.

sections.label: One million MKBF target
sections.summary: The one million MKBF target, set by then-Minister Khaw Boon Wan, remains relevant and valid, though raising it involves cost trade-offs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Indeed, the target of one million was set some years ago, I think by the then-Minister Khaw Boon Wan, as a focus for the One Transport Family to work towards a shared goal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: It is also a meaningful indicator because it allows us to then benchmark against the other operators, especially those who are top of class around the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, the one million was chosen because that represents – and I think it is still relevant today – what the best, most reliable operators, like Taipei, Guangzhou and others, have managed to achieve in their system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: If we look at it today, I think it is still a relevant and valid target, something that is useful for us to focus on and that is something which we will continue to work towards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But whether we should raise it further, I think that is something that we have to assess carefully because there is a trade-off between raising MKBF further and what is the cost incurred, which would then ultimately have to be borne by either taxpayers or commuters.
